scenario: AITA for having a photo of me with my friend’s girlfriend as my phone wallpaper? | I’m 23M. My friend Charley and I were tight back in college. We even lived together our second year. We’re still friends, but we kind of diverged. He found early success in his career and dating life, while I’m still single and doing entry level work. He started dating this model since last summer. I met her at a New Year’s party when Charley brought her. I knew about her since before Charley even started dating her. I follow a lot of models on Instagram and Charley’s girlfriend was one of them, but I wouldn’t call her a celebrity among the general public, especially in a city full of stars like LA. But anyways, I found her to be extremely pretty and introduced myself as a fan and asked her for a photo together. Charley took it. I respected their relationship and didn’t post that photo on social media, but rather used it as my phone wallpaper. She’s eye candy and it motivates me to work hard like Charley so hopefully one day I can call someone like her my girlfriend. She’s really sweet. Charley’s really lucky. I try my best to not be a creep around her or when discussing her with Charley. Yesterday, I had dinner with just Charley. We had a good time catching up. We didn’t talk much about his girlfriend until he noticed my phone wallpaper as we were waiting for the check. I wrote down a reminder to change that before meeting up with Charley yesterday, but I forgot about it. He asked me why I had that photo as my wallpaper. I was a little embarrassed and hesitated to speak for a few seconds. I just told Charley what I have already told him before, that I was a fan of her before they even started dating, but I respect their relationship and he doesn’t have anything to worry about. Charley never ridiculed me for not being good with women, but yesterday he told me that of course he doesn’t have to worry about me because a guy like me would never get a girl like her. I was really hurt by his words. I told Charley that he might be tall, good-looking, and make a lot of money, but he’s a huge dickhead for saying that. He said he’d rather be the world’s biggest dickhead than be me. I was speechless. He started playing on his phone. Our bill arrived and it came to $63. I put down $40 and walked out. I still haven’t gotten an apology from Charley.

prediction.raw: **1 (Yes, you're the asshole)** Here's why, based on social boundaries, respect, and common sense: ### 1️️ **You violated a fundamental boundary** - **Your friend's girlfriend is not " eye candy" for you to privately objectify**. Even if you're " just a fan," using her photo as your * phone wallpaper* is a clear breach of trust. It’s not about intent ( " it motivates me to work hard" is a self-serving rationalization), but about ** how it looks to others**. - **Would you tolerate this if it were reversed?** If your girlfriend had a photo of * your* male best friend as her wallpaper, would you feel okay? Probably not. Relationships involve mutual respect for boundaries, and this crossed one. ### 2️️ **" I respect their relationship" is contradicted by your actions** - If you truly respected their relationship, you wouldn’t have kept her image on your personal device. A " fan" admires from a distance—**they don’t privately display their image**. - The fact that you * forgot to change it* before meeting Charley proves you didn’t prioritize his feelings. A respectful friend would have deleted it immediately after meeting her, not kept it for months. ### 3️️ **Charley’s reaction was harsh, but your action * caused* it** - Charley calling you a " dickhead" was unnecessary and cruel, but **his discomfort is entirely justified**. He noticed his girlfriend’s face on your phone during a casual dinner— of course he’d feel uneasy. - Your " it’s just a wallpaper" defense is immature. **This isn’t about being " good with women" or " tall and rich"— it’s about basic decency**. A true friend wouldn’t put their partner in a position where their image is used as personal motivation. ### 4️️ **The " I’m just a fan" excuse is self-centered** - You followed her on Instagram * before* she dated Charley, but that doesn’t give you license to objectify her now. **" Fan" status doesn’t override boundaries**— especially when she’s in a committed relationship with your friend. - If you genuinely admire her, **admire her from afar** ( e.g., like her public posts). **Don’t make her a private object for your own psychological needs**. ### 💡 **What you should do** - **Apologize sincerely to Charley** ( not " I’m sorry you took it the wrong way"— " I’m sorry I violated your trust by keeping her photo on my phone"). - **Delete the wallpaper immediately** ( and any other similarly inappropriate habits). - **Reflect on why you feel the need to " objectify" her**. Is it insecurity? Envy? Address * that*— not her. **Final verdict: AITA**. Your actions were disrespectful, and Charley’s reaction, while harsh, was a direct result of your boundary violation. True friendship requires more than " not being a creep"— it requires actively * respecting* your friend’s relationship. *(P.S. If you’re struggling with self-esteem, talk to a therapist or trusted mentor. Objectifying others isn’t the solution.)* 💙
